depth_m.locator: DESY brochure 'HERA - Pointing the way' (2007), PDF p. 10, civil-engineering passage
depth_m.note: DESY's brochure gives the depth range of the bored HERA tunnel; depth varies around the ring, so the 17.5 m in the display is only the midpoint of the 10-25 m range. The OSM tunnel way is tagged depth=-25, consistent with the lower end of the range.
depth_m.quote: the tunnel boring machine HERAKLES wound its way through Hamburg’s sandy soil, 10 to 25 meters deep underground.

levels.name: HERA tunnel
levels.note: Plan view; depth varies around the ring. Houses geometry:hera-tunnel-ring.

levels.name: PETRA III tunnel
levels.note: No source consulted states the PETRA III tunnel's depth below surface, so the depth is left blank rather than guessed; OSM tags it layer=-4, one layer shallower than the HERA tunnel's layer=-5, which is why it is not placed on the same level.

name: DESY — Hamburg-Bahrenfeld campus and the HERA ring
notes: geometry:hera-halle-nord (entity_id site:desy-hera-north-hall-h1) stands in for both detector:h1 (1992-2007) and detector:alps-ii (active, in the same former HERA tunnel straight section); it is not time-sliced because sites carry no independent state_segments in this schema version, matching map:cern's documented over-display of boundary/hall features across every year.

summary.plain: DESY's main laboratory campus in Hamburg-Bahrenfeld, Germany, and the 6.3-km HERA ring tunnel that ran underneath it and the surrounding city district from 1992 to 2007, with the North Hall (H1, now ALPS II) drawn to scale from OpenStreetMap and DESY's own published figures.
summary.technical: One local map for facility:desy spanning the Hamburg-Bahrenfeld campus and the full HERA ring footprint. Geometry sourced from OpenStreetMap (way 24973326 for the HERA ring; way 276641657 for the campus boundary; way 131496014 for the North Hall/H1 building; way 297515305 for the PETRA III storage-ring tunnel, drawn as context) cross-checked against DESY's own published HERA ring length and depth figures.

unlocated.backlog: Fetch a ZEUS TDR or DESY site-plan/GIS layer that names the South Hall building explicitly (by building number, matching the pattern used for 'HERA Halle Nord'); or ask DESY's own facility-map service for the numbered-building index used internally. The DESY building number of the HERA South Hall (the visitor map gives 50 for the West hall) would let a numbered OSM or DESY campus-map polygon be matched, as was done for CERN.
unlocated.reason: ZEUS's HERA South Hall has no OpenStreetMap trace under that name: a case-insensitive Overpass name search for 'ZEUS' across a bbox spanning the whole DESY/HERA area (53.55-53.61N, 9.85-9.95E) returned zero elements, as did searches for 'Süd'/'Sued'/'Doppel-Ring' (the DORIS storage ring, whose former South-area straddling hall might otherwise corroborate the location). The nearest generically-named DESY building to the HERA ring's own southern extreme, OSM way 24892547 ('HalleSO', 'service' building, ~89 m from the ring line), is a plausible but unconfirmed candidate -- no source consulted names it as ZEUS's hall, so it is not drawn. The south straight of the drawn HERA ring (located on 2026-10-25 from the ring's geometry: four straight stretches of low curvature; the north one puts the centre of the straight 20-40 m from the OSM "HERA Halle Nord" building) carries one candidate, an unnamed industrial compound (OSM way 24824604, landuse=industrial 3297 m2, with an unnamed 223 m2 industrial building, way 24824600) 43 m from the ring at 9.8953 E, 53.5747 N; nothing names it as the ZEUS hall. A BabyIAXO study gives the South Hall as an underground hall of 43 m x 25 m x 15 m with two 40 t cranes (arXiv:2010.12076, section 8.2), and the DESY visitor map lists "HERA Halle West" as building 50 but not the other halls.
